hyperedges.label: Tufte's Seven Principles of Visual Information Design

nodes.label: Served Personas
nodes.rationale: Used to track second-order social and physical ramifications of products.

nodes.label: Negative Personas
nodes.rationale: Used rhetorically to communicate to the team that a persona should not be the product's design target.

nodes.label: Persona Narrative
nodes.rationale: A synthesis of the most important details observed during research, conveyed as a third-person narrative.

nodes.label: Persona Photo
nodes.rationale: Photographs make personas feel more real and engage the team.

nodes.label: Participatory Design
nodes.rationale: Involving real users in the design process, which can sometimes miss common behaviors across broader sets of users.

nodes.label: Market Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Divides customers based on demographics, unlike personas which are based on behaviors.

nodes.label: Organizational Personas
nodes.rationale: Fictional personas describing the behaviors of organizations.

nodes.label: Provisional Personas
nodes.rationale: Ad hoc personas used when there's not enough data, based on best guesses.

nodes.label: Work Flow Models
nodes.rationale: Used for capturing information flow and decision-making processes inside organizations.

nodes.label: Artifact Models
nodes.rationale: Represent different artifacts users employ in tasks, like forms.

nodes.label: Physical Models
nodes.rationale: Capture the layout of physical objects comprising the user's workspace.

nodes.label: Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Narrative as a design tool to define product behavior from specific users' standpoints.

nodes.label: Use Cases
nodes.rationale: Exhaustive descriptions of system functional requirements, differing from scenario interactions.

nodes.label: User Stories
nodes.rationale: Short sentences phrased for agile programming, lacking the holistic view of scenarios.

nodes.label: Epics
nodes.rationale: Agile method akin to scenarios, describing broader clusters of interactions.

nodes.label: Scenario-Based Design
nodes.rationale: A method of design problem solving by concretization using stories.

nodes.label: User Experience in the Age of Sustainability
nodes.norm_label: user experience in the age of sustainability

nodes.label: Avoid a Fixed Set of Questions
nodes.norm_label: avoid a fixed set of questions

nodes.label: Assume the Role of an Apprentice
nodes.norm_label: assume the role of an apprentice

nodes.label: Research Is Critical to Good Design
nodes.norm_label: research is critical to good design

nodes.label: Icons
nodes.rationale: Icons representing abstract concepts should rely on idioms rather than forced concrete representations. For concrete functions, represent both action and object acted on.

nodes.label: Visually distinguish elements that behave differently
nodes.norm_label: visually distinguish elements that behave differently

nodes.label: Render icons and visual symbols simply
nodes.rationale: Icons should remain simple and schematic, minimizing colors and shades, to avoid drawing undue attention and rendering poorly at small sizes.
nodes.norm_label: render icons and visual symbols simply

nodes.label: Pre-visualize results
nodes.rationale: Use visual elements in addition to text to convey to users what the results of an interface function will be.

nodes.label: Respond to commands
nodes.rationale: Provide visual cues indicating a command was received, depending on the delay length (instant, <1s, 1-10s, >10s).

nodes.label: Draw attention to important events
nodes.rationale: Use contrast (size, color, motion) to draw attention proactively, but avoid misapplying it as it can interrupt the user's current task.

nodes.label: Visual Noise
nodes.rationale: Superfluous visual elements (ornate embellishment, 3D rendering without info, heavy rules, crowding) increase cognitive load and should be minimized.

nodes.label: Keep it simple
nodes.rationale: Visual interfaces should be minimal. Unnecessary variation is the enemy of coherent design.

nodes.label: Take things away until the design breaks
nodes.norm_label: take things away until the design breaks

nodes.label: Seven Grand Principles of Information Design
nodes.norm_label: seven grand principles of information design

nodes.label: Enforce visual comparisons
nodes.rationale: Provide a means for users to compare related variables and trends or to compare before-and-after scenarios.

nodes.label: Show causality
nodes.rationale: Clarify cause and effect within information graphics.

nodes.label: Show multiple variables
nodes.rationale: Data displays should show multiple related variables simultaneously without sacrificing clarity.

nodes.label: Integrate text, graphics, and data in one display
nodes.rationale: Avoid separate keys or legends as they require additional cognitive processing.
nodes.norm_label: integrate text, graphics, and data in one display

nodes.label: Ensure the content's quality, relevance, and integrity
nodes.norm_label: ensure the content's quality, relevance, and integrity

nodes.label: Show things adjacent in space, not stacked in time
nodes.rationale: Changes over time are easier to understand when shown side-by-side rather than superimposed.
nodes.norm_label: show things adjacent in space, not stacked in time

nodes.label: Don't dequantify quantifiable data
nodes.rationale: Do not abandon the display of the numbers themselves even when using graphs and charts.

nodes.label: Interface Consistency and Standards
nodes.rationale: Standards improve users' ability to learn and predict behaviors, but rigid adherence without considering context can force inappropriate interaction models.

nodes.label: Obey standards unless there is a truly superior alternative
nodes.norm_label: obey standards unless there is a truly superior alternative

nodes.label: Design Language
nodes.rationale: A vocabulary of design elements (shape, color, typography) composed to create emotional tone and brand associations.

nodes.label: Primary Navigation
nodes.rationale: Gets user to major areas of a website. Top navigation is superior in most cases.

nodes.label: Secondary Navigation
nodes.rationale: Provides access to content when entire info space cannot be navigated from top-level links.

nodes.label: Breadcrumbs
nodes.rationale: Breadcrumbs with lateral links help speed navigation.

nodes.label: Auto-complete
nodes.rationale: Helps users find things faster.

nodes.label: Auto-suggest
nodes.rationale: Provides search terms based on fuzzy matching.

nodes.label: Faceted Search
nodes.rationale: Allows users to specify attributes of items they are looking for.

nodes.label: Scrolling
nodes.rationale: Make scrolling an engaging experience.

nodes.label: Infinite Scrolling
nodes.rationale: Infinite scroll and site footers are mutually exclusive idioms.

nodes.label: Responsive Web Design
nodes.rationale: If you have only one version of your site, make it responsive.

nodes.label: Imperative Controls
nodes.rationale: Used to initiate a function

nodes.label: Selection Controls
nodes.rationale: Used to select options or data

nodes.label: Entry Controls
nodes.rationale: Used to enter data

nodes.label: Display Controls
nodes.rationale: Used to manipulate display

nodes.label: Buttons
nodes.rationale: The quintessential imperative idiom.

nodes.label: Don't stop the proceedings with idiocy
nodes.norm_label: don't stop the proceedings with idiocy

nodes.label: Allow input wherever you have output
nodes.norm_label: allow input wherever you have output

nodes.label: Hyperlinks
nodes.rationale: Use links for navigation and buttons for action.

nodes.label: Selection Controls
nodes.rationale: Allow user to choose a noun from a group or configure actions.

nodes.label: Check Boxes
nodes.rationale: For single binary choice or selecting from a short list.

nodes.label: Toggle Buttons
nodes.rationale: Superseding check box as single-selection idiom, space-efficient.

nodes.label: State-Switching Buttons
nodes.rationale: Avoid this idiom. Confusion between state indicator and state-switching control.

nodes.label: Radio Buttons
nodes.rationale: Mutually exclusive choices. Use drop-down lists instead for sovereign applications.

nodes.label: Switches
nodes.rationale: Compact version of two radio buttons, used in mobile settings.

nodes.label: Combo Icon Buttons
nodes.rationale: Variant of radio icon button replacing bank of buttons with a drop-down list of icons.

nodes.label: List Controls
nodes.rationale: For selecting from a finite set of text strings.

nodes.label: Barrel Control
nodes.rationale: Gesture-based variant of list control on iOS.

nodes.label: Earmarking
nodes.rationale: Use check boxes in lists to solve multiple selection scrolling issues.

nodes.label: Horizontal Scrolling in Lists
nodes.rationale: Avoid scrolling text horizontally.

nodes.label: Entering Data into a List
nodes.rationale: Edit-in-place facility.

nodes.label: Combo Boxes
nodes.rationale: Combination of a list box and an edit field.

nodes.label: Tree Controls
nodes.rationale: Often inappropriately used. Only use for naturally hierarchical data.

nodes.label: Bounded Entry Controls
nodes.rationale: Use bounded controls for bounded input.

nodes.label: Offer Users a Gallery of Ready-to-Use Templates
nodes.norm_label: offer users a gallery of ready-to-use templates

nodes.label: Full-text search
nodes.rationale: Full-text search is only as complete as the wording of the help text itself, and might not encompass language that reflects users' mental models.

nodes.label: Indexing
nodes.rationale: Creates synonym mappings to map to the user's mental models. Arguably as important as the help text itself.

nodes.label: Overview descriptions
nodes.rationale: Missing ingredient from most online help. Explains fundamental concepts like scope, effect, upside, downside.

nodes.label: In-app user guides
nodes.rationale: Should not be the first line of help, but serve as a reference for detailed information on using complex functions.

nodes.label: Customizability
nodes.rationale: Conundrum between some users' need to have things done their way and the navigation problems this creates.

nodes.label: Personalization
nodes.rationale: Describes the decoration or embellishment of persistent objects without moving them. Helps navigation and makes apps more likable.

nodes.label: Configuration
nodes.rationale: Describes moving, adding, or deleting persistent objects. Valued by corporate IT managers and expert users.

nodes.label: Idiosyncratically modal behavior
nodes.rationale: When the user population splits clearly on preferred idioms, the interface must offer both idioms to satisfy both groups.

nodes.label: Localization
nodes.rationale: Translating an application for a particular language and culture.

nodes.label: Globalization
nodes.rationale: Making an application as universal as possible across many languages and cultures.

nodes.label: Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Designing your app so that it can be effectively used by people with cognitive, sensory, or motor impairments.

nodes.label: Accessibility personas
nodes.rationale: A secondary (or sometimes primary) persona representing someone with special needs to ensure accessibility isn't compromised.

nodes.label: Visual interface design
nodes.rationale: Communicating behavior and information through visual elements, finding the best representation for specific information.

nodes.label: Visual art
nodes.rationale: Means of self-expression on topics of emotional or intellectual concern, without many constraints.

nodes.label: Text Edit Control
nodes.rationale: Simple control allowing users to key in any alphanumeric text value. Should not be used for finite or strictly numeric values without validation.

nodes.label: Validated Entry Control
nodes.rationale: Type of unbounded text-entry control with built-in validation and feedback. Crucial to give users generous, near real-time feedback.

nodes.label: Active Validation
nodes.rationale: Rejects user keystrokes during the entry process if invalid.

nodes.label: Passive Validation
nodes.rationale: Validation takes place only when data reaches a threshold or focus is lost.

nodes.label: Hint
nodes.rationale: Pop-up text explaining acceptable data, appears as soon as control detects invalid character or cursor hovers.

nodes.label: Display Control
nodes.rationale: Manage visual presentation of information onscreen or display read-only info.

nodes.label: Scrollbar
nodes.rationale: Enables small windows to contain large amounts of info. Provides context about location and scale. Overused and demands high mouse precision.

nodes.label: Document Navigator
nodes.rationale: Alternative to scrollbar; uses thumbnail of entire document space to provide direct navigation.

nodes.label: Splitter
nodes.rationale: Divides sovereign application into multiple related panes.

nodes.label: Drawer
nodes.rationale: Pane in sovereign application that opens/closes with a single action, holding less frequently used controls.

nodes.label: Lever
nodes.rationale: Control that swivels to open or close a drawer.

nodes.label: Dialog
nodes.rationale: Pop-up window superimposed over application to offer info and request input. Should play secondary role to main window.

nodes.label: Modal Dialog
nodes.rationale: Stops all proceedings in owning application until closed. Rigidly defined behavior.

nodes.label: Modeless Dialog
nodes.rationale: Allows parent application to continue. More difficult to use because scope of operation is unclear.

nodes.label: Property Dialog
nodes.rationale: Allows users to view and change settings or attributes. Typically modeless.

nodes.label: Function Dialog
nodes.rationale: Usually launched from a menu to control a single function. Most frequently modal. Configures details of action and invokes it.

nodes.label: Design Principle: Dialog Usage
nodes.rationale: Dialogs are appropriate for organizing controls and info about a single domain object or application function. Primary interactions belong in primary window.

nodes.label: Idiomatic Interfaces
nodes.rationale: Focuses on the learning of simple, non-metaphorical visual and behavioral idioms to accomplish tasks, rather than relying on technical knowledge or metaphors.

nodes.label: Interaction Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: A structured set of interaction elements following an inverted pyramid: primitives (bottom), compounds (middle), and idioms (top).

nodes.label: Manual Affordances
nodes.rationale: Instinctive understanding of how objects are manipulated with our hands, based on their shape. Altered from Norman's definition to be purely cognitive.

nodes.label: Direct Manipulation
nodes.rationale: Visual representation and gestural mechanisms for acting on data objects with immediately visible results (coined by Ben Shneiderman).

nodes.label: Pliancy
nodes.rationale: The property of objects or screen areas that react to input and that the user can manipulate directly.

nodes.label: Pliancy Hinting Principle
nodes.rationale: Visually communicate pliancy whenever possible to let users know an object can be manipulated.

nodes.label: Static Hinting
nodes.rationale: Communicating pliancy through the static rendering of the object itself, such as 3D sculpting of a button.

nodes.label: Dynamic Hinting
nodes.rationale: Object temporarily changes appearance when the cursor passes over it (rollover) before any click occurs.

nodes.label: Pliant Response Hinting
nodes.rationale: Visual feedback showing an object is poised to undergo a state change (e.g., button becoming indented when pressed but not yet released).

nodes.label: Cursor Hinting
nodes.rationale: Communicating pliancy by changing the cursor's appearance as it passes over an object or screen area.

nodes.label: Data Integrity (Implementation Model)
nodes.rationale: The imperative of validating all data at point of entry to ensure it is pristine, which places database needs before user needs.

nodes.label: Data Immunity
nodes.rationale: Building applications to handle permutations of data smoothly without rigid validation lockouts, prioritizing human workflow.

nodes.label: Fudgeability
nodes.rationale: The ability of an application to accept exceptions or slightly irregular data to prevent stopping real-world business workflows.

nodes.label: Auditing vs Editing
nodes.rationale: Separating the act of entering data (editing) from the validation of data (auditing) to avoid interrupting the user's flow.

nodes.label: Be generous with screen real estate
nodes.norm_label: be generous with screen real estate

nodes.label: Apple
nodes.rationale: Apple has emphasized desirability but has made many business blunders. Sustained by loyalty created by attention to user experience.

nodes.label: Microsoft
nodes.rationale: Best run businesses ever, but not able to create highly desirable products.

nodes.label: Novell
nodes.rationale: Emphasized technology and gave little attention to desirability.

nodes.label: User Goals
nodes.rationale: Expectation of an end condition, driven by human motivations, change slowly over time.

nodes.label: Tasks
nodes.rationale: Intermediate steps that help someone to reach a goal.

nodes.label: Activities
nodes.rationale: Intermediate steps composed of tasks, changing transiently based on available technology.

nodes.label: Activity-Centered Design (ACD)
nodes.rationale: Focuses on understanding activities, proposed by Donald Norman.

nodes.label: Implementation Model
nodes.rationale: Represents how a machine or application actually works in code.

nodes.label: Mental Model
nodes.rationale: Cognitive shorthand users create for explaining how a mechanism works.

nodes.label: Represented Model
nodes.rationale: How the designer chooses to represent an application's functioning to the user.

nodes.label: Goal-Directed Design
nodes.rationale: Process that meets users' needs and goals while addressing business and technical constraints.

nodes.label: Research Phase
nodes.rationale: Employs ethnographic field study techniques to provide qualitative data.

nodes.label: Modeling Phase
nodes.rationale: Behavior and workflow patterns are synthesized into domain and user models.

nodes.label: Requirements Definition Phase
nodes.rationale: Employs scenario-based design methods focused on meeting goals and needs of specific user personas.

nodes.label: Framework Definition Phase
nodes.rationale: Designers create the overall product concept and synthesize an interaction framework.

nodes.label: Refinement Phase
nodes.rationale: Focus on task coherence and detail using walkthrough scenarios.

nodes.label: Development Support Phase
nodes.rationale: Answering developers' questions during construction process.

nodes.label: Personas
nodes.rationale: Detailed, composite user archetypes that represent distinct groupings of behaviors and goals.

nodes.label: Interaction Design Patterns
nodes.rationale: Encode general solutions to classes of previously analyzed problems.

nodes.label: Context Scenario
nodes.rationale: A day in the life of the persona using the product.

nodes.label: Designing for Three Levels of Experience
nodes.norm_label: designing for three levels of experience

nodes.label: Primary Persona
nodes.rationale: Focus the design for each interface on a single primary persona. Don't make the user feel stupid.

nodes.label: Magic Interface
nodes.rationale: Define what the product will do before you design how the product will do it. In the early stages of design, pretend the interface is magic.

nodes.label: Unified Form and Behavior
nodes.rationale: There is only one user experience: Form and behavior must be designed in concert. Never show a design approach you're unhappy with; stakeholders just might like it.

nodes.label: Considerate Software
nodes.rationale: The computer does the work, and the person does the thinking. Software should behave like a considerate human being. If it's worth it to the user to do it, it's worth it to the application to remember it.

nodes.label: Sovereign Applications
nodes.rationale: Optimize sovereign applications for full-screen use. Sovereign interfaces should feature a conservative visual style. Sovereign applications should exploit rich input. Maximize document views within sovereign applications.

nodes.label: Transient Applications
nodes.rationale: Transient applications must be simple, clear, and to the point. Transient applications should be limited to a single window and view. A transient application should launch to its previous position and configuration.

nodes.label: Optimize for Intermediates
nodes.rationale: Nobody wants to remain a beginner. Optimize for intermediates. Reflect the interface for typical navigation. Imagine users as very intelligent and very busy.

nodes.label: Ask Forgiveness, Not Permission
nodes.rationale: Ask forgiveness, not permission. Don't use dialogs to report normalcy. No matter how cool your interface is, less of it would be better.

nodes.label: Eliminate Excise
nodes.rationale: Eliminate excise wherever possible. Don't stop the proceedings with idiocy. Don't make users ask for permission. Allow input wherever you have output. Significant change must be significantly better.

nodes.label: Direct Manipulation and Idioms
nodes.rationale: All idioms must be learned; good idioms need to be learned only once. Rich visual feedback is the key to successful direct manipulation. Visually communicate pliancy whenever possible.

nodes.label: Audit, Don't Edit
nodes.rationale: Audit, don't edit. Save documents and settings automatically. Put files where users can find them.

nodes.label: Visual Interface Design
nodes.rationale: Visually distinguish elements that behave differently. Visually communicate function and behavior. Visually show what; textually tell which. Obey standards unless there is a truly superior alternative.

nodes.label: Interaction Idioms
nodes.rationale: The utility of any interaction idiom is context-dependent. Provide functions in the window where they are used. Toolbars give experienced users fast access to frequently used functions. Support both mouse and keyboard use for navigation.

nodes.label: Mobile Apps
nodes.rationale: Most mobile apps have transient posture. Limit the number and direction of animated screen transitions. Use guided tours to orient first-time users. Use overlays to explain gestures.

nodes.label: Web Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use persistent headers to maintain context. BREADCRUMS with lateral links help speed navigation. Auto-complete, auto-suggest, and faceted search help users find things faster. Infinite scrolling and site footers are mutually exclusive idioms.

nodes.label: Dialogs and Errors
nodes.rationale: Dialogs are appropriate for functions that are out of the main interaction flow. Most error dialogs stop the proceedings with idiocy. Make errors impossible. Do; don't ask. Make all actions reversible. Provide modeless feedback to help users avoid mistakes.

nodes.label: Let users direct rather than discuss
nodes.norm_label: let users direct rather than discuss

nodes.label: Provide choices rather than ask questions
nodes.norm_label: provide choices rather than ask questions

nodes.label: Keep necessary tools close at hand
nodes.norm_label: keep necessary tools close at hand

nodes.label: Design for the probable but anticipate the possible
nodes.norm_label: design for the probable but anticipate the possible

nodes.label: DESIGN PRINCIPLE: Don't use dialogs to report normalcy
nodes.norm_label: design principle: don't use dialogs to report normalcy

nodes.label: DESIGN PRINCIPLE: Ask for forgiveness, not permission
nodes.norm_label: design principle: ask for forgiveness, not permission

nodes.label: Optimize for responsiveness but accommodate latency
nodes.norm_label: optimize for responsiveness but accommodate latency

nodes.label: DESIGN PRINCIPLE: Eliminate excise wherever possible
nodes.norm_label: design principle: eliminate excise wherever possible

nodes.label: Navigation across multiple screens, views, or pages
nodes.norm_label: navigation across multiple screens, views, or pages

nodes.label: Handheld format apps
nodes.rationale: Eschew complexities of window management for full-screen applications to make better use of limited real estate.

nodes.label: Stacks
nodes.rationale: Vertically organized structures with content area, usually list or grid, with top/bottom bar. Primary pattern for non-game mobile apps.

nodes.label: Screen carousels
nodes.rationale: Alternative top-level pattern for dashboard-like displays. Navigate via horizontal swipe.

nodes.label: Orientation and layout
nodes.rationale: Dynamically rearrange layout for portrait vs landscape. Portrait is usually preferred for one-handed operation.

nodes.label: Tablet format apps
nodes.rationale: More screen real estate allows for complex layouts like index panes and pop-up control panels.

nodes.label: Index panes
nodes.rationale: Additional pane on tablets listing content items to eliminate a level of drill-down.

nodes.label: Pop-up control panels
nodes.rationale: Replace full-screen navigation on tablets. Attached to a specific control with a speech balloon caret.

nodes.label: Desktop-like layout
nodes.rationale: Appropriate for complex productivity/creative apps on tablets.

nodes.label: Mini-tablet format apps
nodes.rationale: Middle ground between phone and tablet; requires careful use of grids, swimlanes, and pop-up dialogs.

nodes.label: Mobile Navigation, Content, and Control Idioms
nodes.norm_label: mobile navigation, content, and control idioms

nodes.label: Browse controls
nodes.rationale: Mobile apps optimized for browsing over data entry.

nodes.label: Lists
nodes.rationale: Most frequently used pattern for handhelds. Can be finite or infinite scrolling.

nodes.label: Grids
nodes.rationale: Organize content like photos or albums into regular rows and columns.

nodes.label: Content carousels
nodes.rationale: Horizontal swipe to navigate objects within a single screen. Should wrap circularly.

nodes.label: Swimlanes
nodes.rationale: Vertical stack of carousels. Combines browsability of carousels with data density of grids.

nodes.label: Cards
nodes.rationale: Self-contained interactive objects combining media, text, links, and social actions.

nodes.label: Bars
nodes.rationale: Narrow horizontal regions for navigating or executing functions.

nodes.label: Tab bars
nodes.rationale: Switch between different list or grid views. Maintain content hierarchy state.

nodes.label: More... controls
nodes.rationale: Overcome limited screen real estate by housing additional navigation or functions.

nodes.label: Tab carousels
nodes.rationale: Horizontally swipable carousel of tabs.

nodes.label: Nav bars and action bars
nodes.rationale: Top-of-screen bars for hierarchy navigation, often including back button and title.

nodes.label: Tool bars and palettes
nodes.rationale: Execute functions on current content. Palettes access tools for documents.

nodes.label: Vertical tool bars
nodes.rationale: Left or right edge tool bars for complex tablet apps.

nodes.label: Persona
nodes.rationale: Multipurpose design tool used to determine product behavior, build consensus, and communicate with stakeholders. It avoids issues like the elastic user, self-referential design, and edge cases.

nodes.label: Elastic User
nodes.rationale: A loosely defined user concept that changes to fit the convenience of the development team.

nodes.label: Self-referential Design
nodes.rationale: When designers or developers project their own goals, motivations, skills, and mental models onto a product.

nodes.label: Edge Cases
nodes.rationale: Situations that might happen but usually won't for most people. Not the primary design target.

nodes.label: User Goal
nodes.rationale: Motivations driving behaviors; the 'why' behind tasks.

nodes.label: Visceral Processing
nodes.rationale: Immediate processing level reacting to visual and sensory aspects. Used for designing visual appearance, motion, and affect.

nodes.label: Behavioral Processing
nodes.rationale: Middle processing level for managing simple everyday behaviors. Primary focus of interaction design.

nodes.label: Reflective Processing
nodes.rationale: Least immediate level of processing involving conscious consideration, memories, and associations. Builds long-term product relationships.

nodes.label: Don't Make the User Feel Stupid
nodes.norm_label: don't make the user feel stupid

nodes.label: Map Interview Subjects to Behavioral Variables
nodes.norm_label: map interview subjects to behavioral variables

nodes.label: Focus the Design for Each Interface on a Single Primary Persona
nodes.norm_label: focus the design for each interface on a single primary persona

nodes.label: Formative Usability Tests
nodes.rationale: Test late enough to be concrete, early enough to allow adjustments. Use personas as guide, test explicitly defined tasks while thinking aloud, use low-tech prototype, minimize bias.

nodes.label: Designer Involvement in Usability
nodes.rationale: Designers should be involved in study planning, observation, and analysis to directly witness user interactions.

nodes.label: Core Teams
nodes.rationale: Small and focused teams arranged around specific expertise, responsible for getting work done efficiently without bloat. Best size is 2 to 4 members.

nodes.label: Extended Teams
nodes.rationale: Large and sometimes geographically distributed, including stakeholders and separate core teams like marketing, design, and engineering.

nodes.label: Thought Partnership
nodes.rationale: A collaborative effort blending generative and synthetic thinking. Partners share goals but approach problems from different angles.

nodes.label: Thinking, Fast and Slow (Daniel Kahneman, Amos Tversky)
nodes.norm_label: thinking, fast and slow (daniel kahneman, amos tversky)

nodes.label: Generator
nodes.rationale: Generates ideas freely, thinks laterally, explores openly. Tends to be concrete thinkers who grab the marker to visualize ideas.

nodes.label: Synthesizer
nodes.rationale: Evaluates, seeks clarity, draws connections, and guides the discussion to ensure user needs are addressed. Focuses on storytelling and asking questions.

nodes.label: 15-Minute Rule
nodes.rationale: If discussion doesn't advance for 15 minutes, bring in an outside designer to probe for rationale and help lift the team out of details.

nodes.label: Scaling Up Excellence (Robert Sutton, Huggy Rao)
nodes.norm_label: scaling up excellence (robert sutton, huggy rao)

nodes.label: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (Edward Tufte)
nodes.norm_label: the visual display of quantitative information (edward tufte)

nodes.label: Designing for the Digital Age (Kim Goodwin)
nodes.norm_label: designing for the digital age (kim goodwin)

nodes.label: Design Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Responsible for users' goals for the product, deciding how it will look, feel, and behave.

nodes.label: Usability Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Responsible for validating that users respond to the design as intended. Focuses on identifying problems.

nodes.label: Engineering Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Responsible for construction, materials, processes, estimating time and cost.

nodes.label: Marketing Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Responsible for defining the market opportunity, customer needs, and inspiring adoption.

nodes.label: Business Leads Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Responsible for defining the business opportunity, prioritizing features, and ensuring profitability.

nodes.label: Agile Development
nodes.rationale: Values speed and iterations. Requires primary elements of an experience to be planned and discussed before being built.

nodes.label: Lean UX (Jeff Gothelf and Josh Seiden)
nodes.norm_label: lean ux (jeff gothelf and josh seiden)

nodes.label: Tool Carousel
nodes.rationale: Combined with tool bars to allow more functions than can fit across the screen. Tames complexity by categorizing tools and letting users swipe horizontally to select.

nodes.label: Menu Bar
nodes.rationale: An idiom to avoid in mobile. Tab bars are preferred. Menu bars hide functionality and lack visual clarity.

nodes.label: Drawer
nodes.rationale: Provides access to a vertical list of navigation elements similar to tabs, using minimal screen real estate by hiding in a panel under the main content area.

nodes.label: Secondary-action Drawer
nodes.rationale: Used to interact with a secondary set of objects, often deployed from the right side of the screen.

nodes.label: Double Drawers
nodes.rationale: Using both a left-hand drawer for primary navigation and a right-hand drawer for secondary actions like messaging.

nodes.label: Item-level Drawer
nodes.rationale: Sliding an individual list or grid item reveals a tool bar for that item. Low discoverability and conflicts with other horizontal gestures.

nodes.label: Limit Animated Screen Transitions
nodes.rationale: Overloading of popping and sliding panes in different directions can be disconcerting and confusing for users.

nodes.label: Tap-to-reveal
nodes.rationale: Allows temporary access to controls (like transport/volume) by tapping the screen, eliminating clutter.

nodes.label: Direct Manipulation
nodes.rationale: Replaces indirect-manipulation idioms (sliders) with gestures on the object being edited. Immersive but requires discovery/learning.

nodes.label: Implicit Sorting
nodes.rationale: Pre-empts user's need to search by utilizing browsing behavior to suggest items.

nodes.label: Voice Search
nodes.rationale: Ease entry for simple searches, though full reliability for general searches is still developing.

nodes.label: Auto-complete
nodes.rationale: Displays a list of popular options matching entered letters to decrease keyboard time.

nodes.label: Tap-ahead
nodes.rationale: Allows taking an auto-suggested term and loading it to refine further.

nodes.label: Auto-suggest
nodes.rationale: Uses fuzzy matching techniques to provide spell-corrected, controlled-vocabulary, and synonym options.

nodes.label: Categorized Suggestions
nodes.rationale: Provides instantaneous suggested options in each category when searching across several types of data.

nodes.label: Sorting and Filtering
nodes.rationale: Merge them into a single set of controls on mobile due to limited space and time.

nodes.label: Welcome and Help Screens
nodes.rationale: Simplest and most effective way to help users learn a mobile interface given the lack of hover states and invisible affordances of gestures.

nodes.label: Guided Tours
nodes.rationale: Carousel of cards explaining functions. Used to orient first-time users.

nodes.label: Overlays
nodes.rationale: Use overlays to explicate gestures. Semitransparent layer on which instructions are displayed.

nodes.label: ToolTip Overlays
nodes.rationale: Attempts to provide a ToolTip-like display of all primary functions on a single overlay screen.

nodes.label: Multi-Touch Gestures
nodes.rationale: Core of mobile experience, utilizing a small vocabulary of gestures for simple discoverability.

nodes.label: Tap
nodes.rationale: Used to select objects and toggle activation state.

nodes.label: Tap-and-hold
nodes.rationale: Falling out of favor due to low discoverability. Used to open contextual pop-up menus.

nodes.label: Drag to Scroll
nodes.rationale: Works horizontally or vertically, a fundamental direct manipulation gesture.

nodes.label: Drag to Move
nodes.rationale: Used to move or copy an object or to move an object arbitrarily within a canvas or grid.

nodes.label: Drag to Control
nodes.rationale: Used to control knobs, switches, sliders, pads, or palette tools.
